note: Automated candidate collection. Not reviewed under this publication's evidence standard. Promote entries to the reviewed radar only through the website's curation process.

items.comparator: Current semiconductor-material development process; Samsung described five years as the current development period. It also cited roughly 50 experiments per month as the practical limit.
items.quantitative_outcome: Samsung's stated targets—not achieved results—were to cut semiconductor-material development time from five years to two years, identify more than five times as many promising candidates, and reduce experiments needed to identify optimal conditions by more than 80%. No realized outcome stated.
items.signal: Samsung described a planned AI system that combines literature, patent and in-house experiment data to generate hypotheses and design experiments. This is a weak signal: the cited advantages are targets, not measured benefits, and the source notes that failed-experiment data and researcher experience remain incompletely digitized.

items.comparator: Holyvolt said its automated lab delivers results 10 times faster than conventional R&D; it did not specify the comparison's methodology or a measured AI-only comparison.
items.quantitative_outcome: The company said its platform's internally consistent dataset covers “more than 500,000 physical cells tested at over 165 million cycles.” It claimed the lab delivers results “10 times faster than conventional R&D,” and that closing the loop with AI lets it “move 100 times faster.” The release does not define the 100-times comparison.
items.signal: A large proprietary battery-cell dataset combined with automated physical testing and a feedback loop is a distinctive data-access and workflow asset. The speed claims are company-reported, not independently evaluated; the funding announcement itself is not counted as evidence.

items.company: TOPPAN Holdings, Aisin, Asahi Kasei, SoftBank, AGC and DIC
items.signal: The six-company consortium announced joint research combining quantum computing, conventional computation and AI for materials development, with plans to compare predictions against measurements from synthesized materials. The partnership could provide distinctive cross-company data access, but no operating benefit or measured result was reported; the project is planned for fiscal 2026–2028.
items.source: NEDO project selection, as reported by Xenospectrum

items.comparator: Enveda’s four human reviewers (almost 26 hours), with human adjudication included in the AI-assisted time; for drafting, Enveda’s manual process (approximately three months).
items.quantitative_outcome: Enveda reported that its system identified all 11 actionable issues found in human review of 1,061 pages of Phase 2 manufacturing batch records. A timed run took just under three hours including human adjudication, versus almost 26 hours for four reviewers—an 89% reduction. Enveda also said Claude generated a first draft of regulatory content in four hours, compared with approximately three months manually.
items.signal: Internal evaluation of AI-assisted GMP batch-record review and regulatory-document drafting showed substantial time savings while retaining expert review. This is a weak competitive-advantage signal: the measured workflow benefit is concrete, but the evaluation was internal and does not establish that it is hard for competitors to reproduce.
items.source: Enveda, in a company announcement carried by Business Wire; the evaluation and results were reported by Enveda.

items.comparator: Side-by-side review of 400 chromatograms under current practice: 90 manual interventions versus 4 with AI/ML-powered peak integration. User testing also compared review speed and user-to-user variability.
items.quantitative_outcome: Waters reported that the 400-chromatogram pilot reduced manual interventions from 90 to 4, a 95% reduction. It also reported 50% faster review and 72% lower user-to-user variability. The cited pilot was with a large pharmaceutical customer; Waters identified its internal pilot as conducted in 2025 and its customer evaluation as conducted in 2026.
items.signal: AI-assisted chromatogram integration showed measured reductions in manual work and review variability in a pharmaceutical QC workflow. This is a weak signal: results are vendor-reported and the source does not show that the capability is difficult for competitors to copy.
items.source: Waters’ launch announcement, distributed by PR Newswire; the reported study was a Waters internal pilot with a global pharmaceutical partner and a Waters customer evaluation.

items.signal: The companies announced Cascade, a planned immune-biology dataset combining 100 million single-cell RNA-seq profiles with more than 11,000 proteomic secretome profiles, across over 150,000 individual and combinatorial cytokine and drug perturbation conditions. The announcement named GSK, Pfizer, Sanofi, Graph Therapeutics, and Turbine as partners. This is a distinctive data-access move that could support AI drug-discovery capabilities; no operating benefit or measured performance outcome was reported.
items.source: Parse Biosciences and Nomic Bio, in a company announcement carried by Business Wire.

items.signal: The companies were reported to be contributing proprietary antibody sequences to a shared developability dataset, with a target of 10,000 antibodies overall and federated infrastructure intended to let members train on combined data without exposing their own sequences. The proposed shared data resource is a distinctive access move for machine-learning-based developability work; the article did not report a measured operating benefit.
items.source: Medspark.ai reported the consortium organized by Ginkgo Bioworks’ Datapoints unit and Apheris.

items.comparator: Google reports comparisons with its predecessor model Argon and an unnamed rival lab’s large frontier model; separate benchmark results compare with other models, but the supplied source does not name all comparators.
items.quantitative_outcome: Google said Gemini 4 Carbon was “more than twice as successful as Argon at writing secure code.” Google’s Chrome team reported it “outperformed a large frontier model from a rival lab by more than 10 times” at generating high-quality patches. The company also reported 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro, 54.8% on ExploitGym, and 71.0% on Collinear’s CWE-bench; results were obtained “with no guardrails in place.”
items.signal: New model benchmark and internal-team results indicate improved secure-code generation and vulnerability discovery, exploitation assessment, and patching. This is a candidate signal, but the reported evidence is company-reported and benchmark-based rather than a demonstrated customer operating benefit.
items.source: SecurityWeek, reporting Google’s announcement and claims

items.signal: Completed all research milestones under an Air Force Phase I SBIR to develop an AI dataset using imagery of foreign object debris/damage on U.S. Air Force and civilian airfields. The imagery collection and dataset work could provide distinctive domain data, but the source states no measured operating benefit or dataset size.
items.source: Safe Pro Group press release via GlobeNewswire, as republished by Yahoo Finance

items.signal: Expanded Army AI work across additional missions and units, including an Army Intelligence Data Platform contract. The announcement says deployments supported faster intelligence and target processing and improved targeting precision, but provides no figures or explicit comparison baseline. The reported contract expansion is a weak adoption signal, not a quantified operating-benefit result.
items.source: Striveworks announcement via PRNewswire, as republished by Yahoo Finance

items.comparator: Legacy H100-based solutions for model training; no baseline specified for manufacturing workflow figures
items.quantitative_outcome: NVIDIA’s case study says: “2.48x faster training on 120B models on DGX GB200 vs. legacy”; Foxconn also reports “25% reduction in production scheduling hours” and a “50% reduction in engineering workload” for injection-molding changeovers. No comparison baseline is stated for the latter two figures.
items.signal: Foxconn reports quantified AI infrastructure and workflow gains alongside use of its FoxBrain model and industrial data. The workflow outcomes are candidates for review, but the source does not explain measurement methods or establish how difficult they are to replicate.
items.source: NVIDIA case study, reporting Foxconn’s results

items.comparator: No measured comparator stated; benefit is an estimate based on preliminary data, specific to the Lekki refinery
items.quantitative_outcome: Honeywell estimates that AI-enabled optimization “could deliver operational benefit of more than 29 cents a barrel” at the Lekki refinery and “more than $60 million in gross benefit per year” at full-capacity throughput. The source labels this an estimate, not a realized measured outcome.
items.signal: A site-specific AI optimization effort pairs the refinery’s operating data with Honeywell’s process expertise. Quantification is preliminary and prospective, so this is a weak candidate rather than a verified result.
items.source: Honeywell Technologies announcement, as reported by Hydrocarbon Processing

items.comparator: No baseline or comparison protocol stated for the AI workflows; the 7% figure is the plant’s annual productivity increase, not an attributed AI comparison
items.quantitative_outcome: Siemens says virtual production preparation “can reduce engineering effort by up to 85 percent and cut time-to-market by up to 40 percent.” Its AI-agent production-planning approach “can enable cost savings of up to 20 percent.” These are stated as potential gains, not reported realized results; the source also states Erlangen has “an annual productivity increase of seven percent” without attributing that figure to the AI workflows.
items.signal: Siemens describes AI and digital-twin workflows tested in its Erlangen factory, but its headline quantified outcomes are potential benefits without a stated baseline or measurement method. Treat as a weak candidate.
